extraction.name: Vibravox
extraction.description: Vibravox is a dataset containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors and an airborne microphone as a reference. It contains over 45 hours per sensor of French speech samples and physiological sounds recorded by 188 participants under different acoustic conditions, along with linguistic transcriptions.
extraction.creator: Julien Hauret; Malo Olivier; Thomas Joubaud; Christophe Langrenne; Sarah Poirée; Véronique Zimpfer; Éric Bavu
extraction.citeAs: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, and Éric Bavu. Vibravox: A Dataset of French Speech Captured with Body-conduction Audio Sensors. 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by having 200 participants wear six different audio sensors (five body-conduction sensors and one airborne reference microphone) while reading sentences sourced from the French Wikipedia subset of Common Voice, and while remaining silent in both quiet and 3D-spatialized noisy environments.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Experiments; Physical data collection; Direct measurement
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some data inconsistencies occurred during collection due to sensors shifting from their initial positions, occasional sensor malfunctions, or instances where a microphone was inadvertently left unequipped.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of 32-bit, 48 kHz audio recordings from six sensors, textual sentences sourced from the French Wikipedia subset of Common Voice, and ambient noise samples sourced from Audio Set and in-house ambisonic recordings of concerts and street events.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Phonetic transcriptions were generated using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA), with a phase of manual phonetic transcription performed for unrecognized words that the automatic phonemizer failed to process correctly.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: text phonemizer of the CoML lab; whisper-timestamped model
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The speech-noisy subset primarily serves testing purposes, as it lacks a clean reference under such conditions; A significant performance drop is observed for the in-ear microphone in noisy conditions, likely due to inadequate acoustic sealing for certain ear canal anatomies that do not fit the sensor properly.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset can support the development of robust communication systems for real-world applications, with potential applications in the military domain, access control, intelligence gathering, and battlefield forensics.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains biometric information (skull and timbre uniqueness, physiological noises like heart rate and breathing) that can be descriptive of a person's identity; data was anonymized and encrypted during storage and analysis to protect participant privacy in accordance with GDPR.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Bandwidth extension (speech enhancement); speech-to-phonemes recognition (automatic speech recognition); speaker verification; developing voice commands; monitoring vital signs including heart rate.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data augmentation was applied, including speed perturbation, pitch shifting, and time masking. Additionally, the speechless-noisy subset was dynamically mixed with the speech-clean subset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A 20 Hz high-pass filter was applied to each audio channel. Text was normalized by lowercasing and removing punctuation except apostrophes. A three-stage automatic filtering process discarded audio samples with a Phoneme Error Rate > 10%, SNR < 1.5 dB, or sensitivity drift. Audio segments were also trimmed by 15 ms to eliminate unwanted artifacts.
